title: Cohort Batcher: KV-Aware Handoff and Fairness Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This note captures an alternative continuous-batching approach that centers cohorts (groups of requests aligned by kernel/kv affinity) rather than pure token- or request-level aggregation. The objective is to get most of the latency/cost benefits of token-level batching while preserving stronger fairness and KV cache locality guarantees for interactive workloads.

Context and motivation:
- Token-level batching maximizes GPU utilization but can starve short interactive requests or break KV cache locality (mixing requests with different prefixes causes cache churn).
- Request-level batching preserves request boundaries (good for fairness) but underutilizes tokens on high-concurrency tails.
- We need a hybrid that: (1) keeps latency SLOs for small chats, (2) amortizes kernel launch + decoding costs across like-requests, (3) preserves KV cache hit-rates for common prefixes, (4) allows graceful degradation for bursty traffic.

Key idea (cohort batching):
- Maintain multiple active cohorts per worker/stream. A cohort is a small FIFO grouping of requests that share a compatibility signature: model-version, quantization/profile, kernel-family, and a short KV affinity fingerprint (first-n token hash, or session tag).
- Requests are assigned to cohorts at arrival time using a lightweight hash + heuristics. Cohorts accept both token- and request-level operations: they batch tokens together for kernel execution but limit cross-request token mixing to preserve prefix cache locality.
- The scheduler operates on cohorts (cohort-queue) instead of single requests, allowing fairness policies and quotas to be enforced at cohort granularity. Cohort sizes are elastic and capped by both a soft token quota and a hard latency window.

Cohort signature composition (suggested):
- model_id::variant
- kernel_family (e.g., flash-attn-v2, tiled-f32)
- kv_affinity_hash = hash(first-4-token-ids || session_id_short || route_tag)
- seq_len_bucket (short/medium/long)

Scheduling primitives:
- CohortQueue: a priority queue of cohorts sorted by (age_score, fairness_score, expected_throughput_gain). Age_score grows linearly with wait time. Fairness_score tracks consumed tokens vs fair share.
- TokenEquityAllocator: periodically computes token credits per cohort to enforce proportional token fairness (prevents a single cohort from monopolizing tokens over time).
- KernelBundler: groups cohorts that are kernel-compatible within a micro-window (2–4ms) to launch a fused kernel call. Bundling prefers cohorts with similar seq_len_bucket to reduce padding waste.
- KV Handoff Gate: before bundling, we check cohort-level KV cache compatibility; if bundling would mix cohorts that risk flushing shared cache lines, we either avoid bundling or mark the execution as KV-isolated.

Operational heuristics and parameters (initial values to test):
- cohort_max_requests = 12
- cohort_max_tokens = 2048
- micro_window_ms = 3
- age_weight = 0.7 (how strongly to prioritize oldest cohorts)
- token_credit_period_ms = 200
- kv_affinity_threshold = 0.85 (probability that two cohorts share enough cache lines to be co-located)

API / runtime changes (minimal):
- Request metadata: optional field kv_hint (string) provided by client to pin cohort affinity (useful for multi-turn or retrieval-augmented flows).
- Runtime metrics per cohort: created_at, last_exec_at, tokens_consumed, cache_hit_estimate. These are strings/numeric in internal metrics but exposed as labels in console.

Pseudocode (high level):
- on_request(req):
    sig = compute_signature(req)
    cohort = enroll_into_existing_or_new(sig)
    cohort.enqueue(req)
    if cohort.tokens >= micro_launch_threshold or cohort.age >= latency_window: schedule_launch(cohort)

- schedule_launch(cohort):
    candidates = gather_compatible_cohorts(cohort, micro_window_ms)
    bundle = KernelBundler.bundle(candidates)
    for b in bundle: allocate_token_credits(b)
    submit_kernel(bundle)

Fairness model: token-equity + age decay
- Each tenant/route/cohort accumulates token_credits. Fast consumers reduce credits. A decaying baseline ensures long-idle users regain priority. This preserves both throughput and short-request latency: small cohorts get boosted age_score so they execute quickly even with low credits.

KV cache strategy:
- Maintain soft KV partitions per cohort family on a worker. Workers attempt to place cohorts with high kv_affinity into same partition to increase reuse.
- Use conservative eviction: KV-aware bundles set an eviction_reserve so that cross-cohort bundles do not evict more than X% of a partition.
- For retrieval-augmented requests the runtime respects client-provided kv_hint to pin to a partition (best-effort across retries).

Kernel selection interplay:
- KernelFamily is a first-class part of cohort signature. Bundler prefers same kernel_family and similar precision/quantization. This avoids kernel switching costs and enables batched int8 paths.
- We suggest exposing per-cohort preferred kernel_profile in telemetry so model-onboarding can specify friendly kernels.

Metrics to measure (experiments):
- p50/p95/p99 latency per route, split by short vs long prefixes
- KV cache hit rate (per partner/route)
- token utilization (GPU tokens/sec), kernel fusion ratio
- cohort churn (how often cohorts flush or reassign)

A/B experiment plan:
- Canary stage: deploy cohort-batcher on a single sharded pool behind traffic % ramp (start 2%). Compare against baseline continuous-token-batcher on same traffic.
- Observe: tail latency on interactive routes, token throughput, KV hit rate, error rates.
- Ramp decisions: if p99 tail for small requests increases >10% in 5m window, rollback. If token throughput improves >8% and KV hit no worse than -2%, continue ramp.

Rollout considerations and migration path:
- Start as an opt-in routing policy in the control plane per-route. Customers can mark routes as cohort-friendly (or provide kv_hint).
- Default to cohort batching only on routes with >X samples of repeated prefixes to avoid regressions for fully random workloads.

Open questions and risks:
- How to set kv_affinity_threshold robustly across languages and tokenizers? (need dataset experiments)
- Cohort explosion: pathological streams could create many single-request cohorts; need eviction/merge heuristics.
- Fairness tuning: token-equity parameters interact with autoscaling and dedicated capacity allocation (billing fairness concerns).

Immediate next steps / experiments:
- Build local simulator that models cohorts, kernels, and KV hit dynamics. Run against recorded traffic traces (chat sessions + RAG) to sweep parameters micro_window_ms, cohort_size, kv_threshold.
- Prototype KernelBundler with two kernel_families (flash-attn-v2 and tiled-f32) and measure fusion overheads on small batches.
- Add a lightweight kv_hint header to internal SDK for canary customers to opt-in.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally pragmatic: avoid a giant global scheduler. CohortQueue lives per-worker and coordinates with global routing only for capacity signals.
- I expect many tuning knobs; the goal of this doc is to capture the primitives and an experimental path rather than fixed numbers.

Tagged follow-ups:
- UX: console should show cohort-level telemetry (hot prefixes, affinity partitions)
- Billing: ensure token-equity doesn't create surprises for committed capacity customers (map cohorts -> tenant in accounting)
- Security: cohort isolation must preserve tenant data separation for private deployments (no shared KV partitions across tenants).
summary: Draft design for a cohort-based continuous batcher that balances token efficiency, KV cache locality, and fairness through cohort-level queues, token equity, and kernel bundling.
